articles.title: Unit-Testing an Hreflang Map Generated From a Spreadsheet
articles.excerpt: Many multilingual sites still maintain language alternates in a spreadsheet. Generating hreflang tags or an XML sitemap from that sheet is fine — shipping without tests is not. Broken return links and…
articles.body: Many multilingual sites still maintain language alternates in a spreadsheet. Generating hreflang tags or an XML sitemap from that sheet is fine — shipping without tests is not. Broken return links and missing x-default are silent until an audit. Treat the sheet as a fixture Export a frozen CSV into the repo. Columns: path , locale , canonical_host . Generation code reads only that file in tests so a live sheet edit cannot flake CI. Assert reciprocity For every URL A that points to B as zh-CN , B must point back to A as the correct locale. Write one test that builds the full map and checks both directions. Fail with the pair of URLs, not a boolean. Assert x-default policy Decide whether x-default is the English page, a chooser page or omitted.

The bug report says calculateTotal() crashes on an empty order, and the fix is a guard clause at the top of the function. The branch the agent hands back touches seven files. The guard clause is in there. So is amt renamed to amount at every call site, the imports in cart.ts sorted, and the discount logic next door pulled out into a helper "for readability." The tests pass. The summary says done. Now you're the reviewer. Which of those lines is the fix?

articles.title: A Robots.txt Matrix for AI Crawlers: Allow, Delay or Block by Bot
articles.excerpt: Different AI crawlers honour robots.txt in different ways, and a single Disallow: / aimed at one vendor can accidentally silence another that your GEO programme cares about. A small matrix in version…
articles.body: Different AI crawlers honour robots.txt in different ways, and a single Disallow: / aimed at one vendor can accidentally silence another that your GEO programme cares about. A small matrix in version control beats tribal knowledge in Slack. Inventory the bots you actually see From two weeks of access logs, list user-agents that look like AI or training crawlers. Common ones change over time, so do not copy a blog post from last year blindly. Note path volume and status codes for each. Decide per bot, not globally For each bot, pick one policy: allow all public content, allow only /blog and docs, crawl-delay if supported, or block. Training crawlers and live-answer crawlers are different products; treating them the same is a business decision, not a default.

articles.body: A public case study asks a reader to infer something about your work. The structure should make that inference inspectable. A diagram can explain a design without proving deployment. A passing test suite can support software behavior without establishing usefulness. A strong metric can still describe a weak target. When I updated my portfolio with recent AI-assisted technical work, I wanted each case to connect its claim to the available evidence and to the limits of that evidence. This is a publishing practice, not a new experiment or a claim of independent personal mastery. Name the claim before selecting the artifact Different claims need different support. “Implemented a retrieval path” calls for execution evidence and clear component boundaries.

articles.body: On Episode 234 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Mike Wall are joined by Than Putzig of the Planetary Science Institute about a NASA-backed payload bound for the Marius Hills Pit on the moon. In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? Could Marius Hills Pit, a roughly 50-meter-wide opening that may lead into a lunar lava tube, become the Moon's first living habitat for humans? Putzig explains how geophysical instruments on a rover could detect hidden voids beneath the surface and measure the size of these lava tubes.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.title: Betelgeuse is haunted by a cosmic poltergeist tormenting the doomed star's atmosphere
articles.excerpt: Radio images show the supergiant's atmosphere recovering from its dramatic dimming, while a companion plows through its outer layers.
articles.body: Something spooky is stirring in the shadows of the infamous star Betelgeuse, a cosmic poltergeist that is disrupting the atmosphere of the red supergiant. New radio observations have shown Betelgeuse's smaller stellar companion, Siwarha (not Betelguese Betelguese, unfortunately), cutting through the supergiant's extended atmosphere and leaving a wake in its path, like a jet boat slicing through a lake.

articles.title: Halloween night sky 2026 — Saturn, shooting stars and a space station await US stargazers
articles.excerpt: From Saturn's spectacular rings to Halloween fireballs and a space station flyover, there are plenty of celestial treats in store this Halloween. Here's when and where to look.
articles.body: There could be more than just ghosts and ghouls lurking in the skies this Halloween! From Saturn's spectacular rings to shooting stars and even a space station flyover, the night sky has a few treats of its own in store for U.S. skywatchers on Oct. 31. Based on the latest national forecast, skies will be mainly clear on Saturday evening over most of New York State, northeast Pennsylvania, northern New Jersey and New England as well as a swath of the southern and central Great Plains, central Rockies, a portion of the Pacific Northwest and central and south Florida, as costumed kids arrive at the door looking for candy or some other Halloween treat.

articles.title: Happy Halloween! SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites to orbit from California (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX sent another batch of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit from California just after midnight on Halloween (Oct. 31).
articles.body: SpaceX celebrated Halloween with an early-morning launch from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today (Oct. 31) at 12:04 a.m. EDT (0404 GMT; 9:04 p.m. on Oct. 30 local time), sending 27 of the company's Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO). The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth as planned, touching down about 8.5 minutes after launch on the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base just after midnight ET on Oct. 31, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) It was the 18th flight for this particular booster, which is designated B1093.
